title: 04 Assemble the archive package for NCEI
text:
Status
The package layout below is a proposal to agree with NCEI and with Matt Biddle and Enrique Montes, who are already working on NCEI publication of EcoTaxa data (the SECOORA LOI also names FathomNet in that work). It is BagIt-style because a checksummed, self-describing bag survives any transport. Which route NCEI prefers (Send2NCEI for a one-off, ATRAC with a submission agreement for a recurring flow, or a FathomNet-mediated path) and which metadata profile the imaging pipeline requires are the first questions for them; nothing here is an NCEI decision, and nothing here submits.

title: 04 Assemble the archive package for NCEI
section: What a submission would then look like (assumption, to agree)
text:
What a submission would then look like (assumption, to agree)

Copy the bag to the staging bucket (egress-free object storage; a public copy via NODD if NOAA wants one), under ecotaxa/{dataset_key}/{version}/.
Send NCEI the bag’s location and bag-info.txt through the agreed route (S2N for a pilot; ATRAC with a submission agreement for the recurring flow). The ISO 19115-2 record NCEI needs would be generated from the same EML with NCEI’s template once the profile is agreed; data/metadata/dataset.json holds the ACDD-style attributes it would draw on.
On accession, write the accession number and DOI back into the project’s EML, so the next DwC-A version cites the archived copy.
A re-validation or a new cruise makes a new version; a submitted version is never edited.

title: 02 Categories to WoRMS
text:
EcoTaxa’s taxonomy is WoRMS now
Since its 2026 major version EcoTaxa uses the WoRMS taxonomy: every phylogenetic category carries an AphiaID and a WoRMS lineage, deprecated categories were remapped (Ifremer publishes the list), and the API has a taxon_set/wormsification call that maps any category, morphological ones included, to its nearest WoRMS taxon. The TSV export still carries the category’s name, EcoTaxa id and lineage rather than the AphiaID, so this notebook resolves each distinct category once, through the node’s taxonomy, into a table a person can review. EcoTaxa’s own mapping is shown beside the decision as a cross-check.

title: EcoTaxa to OBIS and NCEI: a working demo
text:
The notebooks



Notebook
What it does
Reusable logic




01 Export
pulls the project through the REST API (token login, general export job, TSV + images), caches it under data/
R/ecotaxa_api.R


02 Taxa
resolves every EcoTaxa category to WoRMS into a reviewable lookup table, with explicit rules for non-living and morphological categories
R/taxa.R


03 OBIS
builds Event, Occurrence and eMoF, the EML and meta.xml, zips a Darwin Core Archive, validates it (obistools)
R/dwc.R, R/eml.R


04 NCEI
assembles a BagIt-style archive package (images, TSV, DwC-A, metadata, SHA-256 manifest) and verifies it; describes the submission route as a proposal
R/ncei.R



Every rule in R/ has a testthat test on a small synthetic fixture (tests/testthat/); run them with Rscript tests/run_tests.R. The notebooks call the functions, the tests assert them, so the two cannot drift.

title: EcoTaxa to OBIS and NCEI: a working demo
text:
Where it comes from
The structure borrows from the CalCOFI Darwin Core pipeline (publish notebooks, calcofi4db): a term map that drives meta.xml so a column without a term is an error; vocabulary ids filled only on an exact match, never invented; deterministic archives with a content hash; and findings that gate the build instead of warnings that scroll by.

title: EcoTaxa to OBIS and NCEI: a working demo
text:
Honest limits of the demo

The demo project’s eight objects are all predicted by the classifier, none validated. The OBIS notebook therefore opts in to predicted objects (include_predicted = TRUE) and the archive carries identificationVerificationStatus = predicted on every occurrence. A real publication would not.
EcoTaxa’s taxonomy is WoRMS since its 2026 major version, so the two phylogenetic categories (Cyclopoida, Oncaeidae) carry an AphiaID and publish. The four morphological ones (detritus, other, egg, t001) are excluded by rule; EcoTaxa’s own mapping would publish egg and other as Biota and drop the other two (notebook 02 shows the cross-check).
The NERC P01 ids in metadata/measurement_type.csv are filled only where the concept is exact; most are empty on purpose and show up as no_measurement_type_id warnings.
The NCEI package layout and route are a proposal to agree with NCEI, not an NCEI specification.

text:
What this does
EcoTaxa’s REST API ({ECOTAXA_URL}/api/docs) exposes a general export job: it writes a zip with one TSV per sample (object, sample, acquisition and process fields, plus each object’s category, annotation status, annotator and date) and, optionally, the images. This notebook logs in with a token, starts the job for project 2, waits for it, downloads and unzips it under data/export/, and reads the TSVs into one objects table cached as Parquet. Later notebooks read the cache and never touch the node.
Credentials come from a git-ignored .Renviron (ECOTAXA_URL, ECOTAXA_USER, ECOTAXA_PASSWORD). When no login is configured, the notebook falls back to the upstream test set in data-raw/import_test/, which is the byte-identical source of project 2’s eight objects (see data-raw/README.md), so the rest of the pipeline still runs on the same data; it says so below.


Code
librarian::shelf(httr2, dplyr, readr, tibble, arrow, jsonlite, here, quiet = TRUE)
for (f in list.files(here("R"), pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
PROJECT_ID <- 2L
DIR_EXPORT <- here("data/export", paste0("project-", PROJECT_ID))
dir.create(DIR_EXPORT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

title: 01 Export a project from EcoTaxa
text:
Notes

The export carries object_annotation_category_id, the node’s internal taxonomy id, which notebook 02 resolves. It carries no AphiaID.
A login token from POST /api/login is a JWT; the API also offers /token with a refresh token, which a scheduled pipeline should prefer.
with_images = "first" ships the visible image per object; "all" can produce several TSV lines per object.

title: 03 Build and validate the Darwin Core Archive for OBIS
text:
What this does
From the cached export (01) and the reviewed lookup (02): one Event per sample (a child event per acquisition when a sample has several), Occurrence rows for validated objects aggregated per event and taxon, an extended MeasurementOrFact with the instrument (NERC L22 URI from the node), the sample volume, the object count, the concentration where a volume exists and the mean equivalent spherical diameter as exported, then EML, meta.xml, a deterministic DwC-A zip with a manifest, and the checks.
The upload to the OBIS-USA IPT stays a deliberate manual act by the data owner. Nothing here talks to a portal.


Code
librarian::shelf(dplyr, readr, tibble, arrow, jsonlite, xml2, digest, obistools, here, quiet = TRUE)

DATASET_KEY <- paste0("ecotaxa-om-prj", PROJECT_ID)
VERSION     <- format(Sys.Date())
DIR_EXPORT  <- here("data/export", paste0("project-", PROJECT_ID))
DIR_DWCA    <- here("data/darwincore", DATASET_KEY)
objects <- read_parquet(file.path(DIR_EXPORT, "objects.parquet"))
lookup  <- read_taxa_lookup(here("metadata/taxa_lookup.csv"))
reg     <- read_measurement_registry(here("metadata/measurement_type.csv"))
project <- ecotaxa_projects() |> filter(projid == PROJECT_ID)

text:
Next, by a person

Review metadata/taxa_lookup.csv and the predicted_included finding above.
Upload ecotaxa-om-prj2_2026-11-06.zip to the OBIS-USA IPT as a new resource (or a new version of one) and record the IPT resource id and the OBIS dataset id in the manifest; OBIS harvests the IPT and the record reaches GBIF through OBIS-USA.
Compare with EcoTaxa’s own collections/export/darwin_core output for the same project as a cross-check.
